newsitem.title: USA: Cyclone picking up speed again off Queensland - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone picking up speed again off Queensland - WSC.

text.p: Tropical Cyclone Justin is picking up speed and may threaten the coast of Queensland, Australia, independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday.

The cyclone, with 100 mph winds, is in the Coral Sea, east of Queensland, near 12.4s/153.0e and is moving west-southwest at 10 mph. It has reached peak intensity and should begin to weaken slowly, WSC said.

During the next 48 hours it will turn more to the southwest then south, but may be nearing the coast of Queensland in the vicinity of Mackay by that time. Justin will bring the threat of heavy rain and strong wind to the coast late in this period, and will be a threat to shipping.
The cyclone had been expected to move towards the Queensland coast last week but stayed at sea and began to weaken.
